results.root_cause_actual: PR #881 raised the payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s and disabled the circuit breaker. When partner acquirer latency spiked to 12.4s p99, all 64 shared gateway worker threads became blocked waiting on payments-svc responses for up to 30s (far exceeding the ALB's 10s proxy_read_timeout), exhausting the thread pool and causing all routes—including those unrelated to payments—to fail with 504s.
results.root_cause_expected: PR #881 raised the gateway's payments-svc read timeout from 3s to 30s (and disabled the circuit breaker) while the edge load balancer's proxy_read_timeout stayed at 10s. When partner latency rose, the edge cut clients off at 10s with 504s while gateway worker threads stayed pinned on the upstream call for the full 30s, saturating the 64-thread pool and taking down routes that never touch payments-svc.

judge.reason: Both identify the same underlying cause: PR #881's timeout mismatch (30s gateway timeout exceeding 10s edge timeout) combined with disabling the circuit breaker, which caused worker thread exhaustion when partner latency increased, affecting all routes.

evidence_cited: PAYMENTS_CIRCUIT_BREAKER  enabled -> disabled  (breaker tripped too often at 3s)
